reason: B swaps Capital One's React/Electron test-data tool bullet, which is frontend and off-target for infra, for a UMD Nano-Satellite 'Systems Engineer' bullet about GraphQL interfaces to KubOS that stream health telemetry. That bullet is loosely observability-adjacent, but it is thin and the claim is vague: it is unclear how GraphQL cut 'communication latency 23%' or what the baseline was. It adds little beyond the stronger Kinesis/Lambda, CDK and Redis evidence already on the page. A keeps a credible, metric-backed bullet (90% of 30+ developers preferred it) that shows shipping and testing (Jest), and it avoids stretching the candidate further, so a panel would slightly prefer A.
risk_noted: The Nano-Satellite role makes four concurrent 'Present' roles (Amazon Leo contract, UMIACS, Nano-Satellite, TerpLabs), all College Park-based, overlapping a full-time Sep-Dec 2026 AWS internship in Redmond. A skeptic will question the depth and real time commitment of each. The single vague GraphQL latency metric also invites scrutiny, and the satellite domain slightly dilutes the cloud/distributed-systems story.
